rv.q: With striking design work and deft delivery of the play’s unconventional dialogue, TUTA’s production offers an intriguing yet confounding experience that puts up literal and figurative barriers between characters and audience.
This thoughtful, provoking piece, despite the darkness of the message, left me with a feeling of awe of what theater can do.
That connection between performer and audience is, to me, what defines theatre—and Tom & Eliza is an exemplar of it.
Frei and Park keep the dialogue taut and engaging, even as they mostly don't move from their stools.
"Tom & Eliza" is a fairly brilliant example of absurdist theater.

cn.t: Critics praise this brilliantly absurd exploration of marriage and aging, with standout performances by Clifton Frei and Seoyoung Park bringing Celine Song's existential vision to vivid life under Aileen Wen McGroddy's expert direction.
